doshaProfile.awaitBody: Discover your unique Ayurvedic constitution through our guided quiz and unlock personalized wellness insights.
doshaProfile.ch1Lede: The elements, qualities, and patterns that shape your constitution.
doshaProfile.footnoteTridoshic: A rare and balanced constitution. All three doshas are equally expressed in your nature.
doshaProfile.footnoteDual: You express {{primary}} and {{secondary}} almost equally. Your constitution shifts with seasons and lifestyle.
doshaProfile.footnoteGapHigh: {{primary}} is overwhelmingly dominant in your constitution. The other doshas play a minor supporting role.
doshaProfile.footnoteGapMid: {{primary}} is clearly your leading dosha. {{secondary}} ({{pct}}%) plays a moderate background role.
doshaProfile.footnoteGapLow: {{primary}} leads your constitution, with {{secondary}} ({{pct}}%) as a notable secondary influence.
doshaProfile.bodySummary: Build, skin, hair, digestion, sleep, energy
doshaProfile.mindSummary: How you show up — at your best and when you're off
doshaProfile.ch2Lede: Early signs of imbalance, common triggers, and Charaka's guidance for returning to centre.
doshaProfile.signsIntro: When your dominant dosha runs high, these are the early signals. None require alarm — they're invitations to lean into the balancing practices below.
doshaProfile.triggersSummary: Habits and seasons that push you out of balance
doshaProfile.pacifySummaryFallback: Lifestyle adjustments to pacify your dosha
doshaProfile.ch3Lede: Translate this knowledge into daily life — the season, the hour of the day, the food on your plate.
doshaProfile.teaserBody: Your season-by-season protocol, dosha-aware diet, and full Dinacharya — the daily rituals that translate Ayurveda into how you actually live.
doshaProfile.unlockChapter3Aria: Unlock Chapter 3 — Live by your dosha
doshaProfile.peakSeasonBody: {{season}} — {{name}} is naturally elevated during this time. Extra care is needed to stay balanced.
doshaProfile.doshaHoursBody: {{timeOfDay}} — These are the hours when {{name}} energy peaks in the body.
doshaProfile.protocolBody: Food, movement, breath, and rest — for the days when your dominant dosha is also your imbalance.
doshaProfile.dietSummary: Foods to favor and avoid, by the six tastes
doshaProfile.routineSummary: Charaka's 13 practices — align the day with the body's rhythm
doshaProfile.understandingBody: In Ayurveda, your Prakriti is your birth constitution — the unique ratio of Vata, Pitta, and Kapha you were born with. It remains stable throughout life. When doshas shift due to diet, stress, or seasons, that temporary state is called Vikriti. The goal of Ayurveda is to bring Vikriti back in alignment with Prakriti.
doshaProfile.paywallSubhead: Unlock Chapter 3 and your full Ayurvedic lifestyle protocol.

morning: Checking your phone before getting out of bed

quotes.0: Health is a state of complete harmony of the body, mind, and spirit.
quotes.1: Yoga is not about touching your toes. It is about what you learn on the way down.
quotes.2: The rhythm of the body, the melody of the mind, and the harmony of the soul create the symphony of life.
quotes.3: When the breath wanders, the mind is also unsteady. But when the breath is calmed, the mind too will be still.
quotes.4: Yoga does not just change the way we see things, it transforms the person who sees.
quotes.5: The body is your temple. Keep it pure and clean for the soul to reside in.
quotes.6: An ounce of practice is worth more than tons of preaching.
quotes.7: When diet is wrong, medicine is of no use. When diet is correct, medicine is of no need.
quotes.8: The part can never be well unless the whole is well.
quotes.9: Every human being is the author of his own health or disease.
quotes.10: The natural healing force within each of us is the greatest force in getting well.
quotes.11: True peace is not the absence of movement, but the stillness at the heart of it.
quotes.12: He who has health has hope, and he who has hope has everything.
quotes.13: The soul is the same in all living creatures, although the body of each is different.
quotes.14: Yoga is the cessation of the movements of the mind. Then there is abiding in the Seer's own form.
quotes.15: With your practice as the foundation, you can move mountains within.
quotes.16: Undisturbed calmness of mind is attained by cultivating friendliness toward the happy, compassion for the unhappy, delight in the virtuous, and indifference toward the wicked.
quotes.17: Arise, awake, and stop not until the goal is reached.
quotes.18: In a conflict between the heart and the brain, follow your heart.
quotes.19: All the powers in the universe are already ours. It is we who have put our hands before our eyes and cry that it is dark.
quotes.20: The greatest sin is to think that you are weak.
quotes.21: You have the right to work, but never to the fruit of the work. Be not attached to inaction.
quotes.22: Reshape yourself through the power of your will. Those who have conquered themselves live in peace, alike in cold and heat, pleasure and pain.
quotes.23: The mind is restless and difficult to restrain, but it is subdued by practice.
quotes.24: When meditation is mastered, the mind is unwavering like the flame of a candle in a windless place.
quotes.25: Almost everything will work again if you unplug it for a few minutes, including you.
quotes.26: Silence is not empty, it is full of answers.
quotes.27: The wound is the place where the light enters you.
quotes.28: What you seek is seeking you.
quotes.29: The quieter you become, the more you are able to hear.
quotes.30: Do not feel lonely; the entire universe is inside you.
quotes.31: A person whose doshas are in balance, whose appetite is good, whose tissues are functioning normally, and whose mind and senses remain full of bliss, is called a healthy person.
quotes.32: The three pillars of life are food, sleep, and the observance of celibacy. Being supported by these three, the body is endowed with strength.
quotes.33: He whose doshas are in equilibrium, whose digestion is good, who acts virtuously — he is said to be healthy.
quotes.34: Prevention is better than cure. The wise man adapts himself before illness arrives.
quotes.35: The food you eat can be either the safest and most powerful form of medicine, or the slowest form of poison.
quotes.36: You are what your deep, driving desire is. As your desire is, so is your will. As your will is, so is your deed. As your deed is, so is your destiny.
quotes.37: From the unreal, lead me to the real. From darkness, lead me to light. From death, lead me to immortality.
quotes.38: As the rivers flowing east and west merge in the sea and become one with it, forgetting they were ever separate rivers, so do all creatures lose their separateness when they merge into pure being.
quotes.39: Feelings come and go like clouds in a windy sky. Conscious breathing is my anchor.
quotes.41: Walk as if you are kissing the Earth with your feet.
quotes.42: Look deep into nature, and then you will understand everything better.
quotes.43: The doctor of the future will give no medicine, but will interest his patients in the care of the human frame, diet, and the cause and prevention of disease.
quotes.44: Rest is not idleness, and to lie sometimes on the grass under trees on a summer's day is by no means a waste of time.
quotes.45: Nature does not hurry, yet everything is accomplished.
quotes.46: The journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
quotes.47: To keep the body in good health is a duty, otherwise we shall not be able to keep our mind strong and clear.
quotes.48: Peace comes from within. Do not seek it without.
quotes.49: In the middle of difficulty lies opportunity.

notifications.dailyReadyBody: A session made for your {{slot}}. Take a few minutes for yourself.
notifications.streakSaveBody: You’re on a {{days}}-day streak. A short practice keeps it going.
notifications.windDownBody: An evening session to help you unwind and prepare for rest.
notifications.vikritiDueBody: A quick check-in keeps your practice tuned to you.

reminderPrompt.title: Never miss your practice

diet.sectionSubtitle: How a food acts on your doshas — from the classical texts, checked by a human.
diet.searchPlaceholder: Search a food — rice, ghee, coffee…

miss.title: Not in our reference yet
miss.body: We don't have reliable Ayurvedic guidance on this food yet, and we'd rather say so than guess. Every entry here is checked against the classical texts by a person before it appears.

diet.derived: Derived from its properties — not classically cited
diet.noTarget: Take the dosha quiz and we'll tell you what this means for you specifically.
diet.targetExplained: Your constitution is {{prakriti}}, but lately you've been running {{vikriti}}-high — so we're reading this against {{vikriti}}.

excluded.allergen: Contains {{key}}. You've told us this is an allergen for you, so this food is excluded from anything we suggest.
excluded.uncertified: We can't confirm whether this is {{key}}, so we've left it out rather than imply it's been checked.

diet.balancedByHelp: Traditionally used to make this food easier to digest. Suggestions, never requirements — nothing here is filtered out if you skip them.

verdict.caution: Go easy on this right now

dietPrefs.title: Food to keep off your plate
dietPrefs.intro: Anything you record here is removed from every food suggestion we make — not ranked lower, removed. You can change it any time.
dietPrefs.allergensHelp: Treated as an absolute filter. An Ayurvedic “favour this” never overrides an allergy.
dietPrefs.patternsHelp: Preferences and observances. Filtered the same way, but described as a choice rather than a safety limit.
dietPrefs.notSetYet: Nothing recorded yet. An empty list means you haven't told us — not that nothing applies.
dietPrefs.syncFailed: We couldn't sync this to your account, so it's saved on this device only. Your filter still works here. We'll retry next time you open the app.
dietPrefs.notExhaustive: This list covers the most common restrictions, not every possible one. If something you need isn't here, please check ingredients yourself — we'd rather say that plainly than let the list imply it's complete.
dietPrefs.consentNeededHint: Agree above and we'll save that — until then nothing about your health leaves this screen.
dietPrefs.eatingStyleHelp: Pick the one that fits — it sets which animal foods you’re shown.
dietPrefs.observancesHelp: Any that apply — these stack on top of your eating style.

meals.title: Meal guidance
meals.plusPitch: Meal ideas tuned to your current imbalance, the season, and what you can't eat — composed from the same reviewed sources as everything else here.
meals.paywallHeadline: Eat for how you are today
meals.paywallSubhead: Meal ideas that follow your imbalance and your restrictions, not a generic plan.
meals.noTarget: Take the dosha quiz and these become specific to you. For now, these are simply well-made seasonal meals.
meals.notRecipes: These are meal ideas, not recipes — no quantities and no method. Cook them the way you already cook.

filtered.title: Nothing we can safely suggest
filtered.body: We had ideas for right now, but every one of them contains something you've asked us to exclude. We'd rather show you nothing than drop one of your restrictions to fill the page.

unreviewed.title: Not ready yet
unreviewed.body: Our meal ideas are still being checked by a person before they go live. That's our work to finish — the food search below is already reviewed and available.

meals.entryHelp: Meal ideas for your imbalance · Plus

mealCheck.title: Meal Check
mealCheck.inputHelp: Tell me what you ate — I'll show how it moves your doshas.
mealCheck.inputPlaceholder: e.g. eggs with toast and avocado
mealCheck.confirmHelp: Tap a food to remove it, or add anything we missed.
mealCheck.noItemsYet: No foods yet — add one below.
mealCheck.dontHave: We don't have "{{token}}" yet — pick the closest, or skip it.
mealCheck.verdictBalanced: This meal is broadly balanced for you.
mealCheck.verdictMind: This meal raises {{dosha}} — your dominant dosha, so worth easing off.
mealCheck.verdictWatch: This meal raises {{dosha}} — keep an eye if you run high there.
mealCheck.disclaimer: A wellness guide, not medical advice.
mealCheck.lockedBody: See how any meal moves your doshas — and how to rebalance. Part of Plus.
mealCheck.swipeHint: Swipe a check left to delete it.
mealCheck.addNotFound: Not in our foods yet — try another word.
mealCheck.effectOnlyLabel: This meal’s effect on your doshas
mealCheck.meansMind: You run {{dosha}} — {{element}}. This meal adds to it, and left unchecked that can surface as {{surface}} later.
mealCheck.meansWatch: This nudges your {{dosha}} up. It isn’t your dominant dosha, so it’s usually mild — ease it if you feel it.
mealCheck.meansGood: This settles {{dosha}} — supportive for how you’re running right now.
mealCheck.meansBalanced: Nothing here pulls you off balance — a steady plate for your constitution.
mealCheck.eatDrinkPitta: Eat or drink to cool it
mealCheck.eatDrinkKapha: Eat or drink to lighten it
mealCheck.eatDrinkVata: Eat or drink to ground it
mealCheck.breatheTitle: Or take a few minutes to breathe
mealCheck.rebalanceWhyMind: Because you run {{dosha}} and this meal pushed it up further — these bring it back toward balance.
mealCheck.rebalanceWhyWatch: This nudged {{dosha}} up. These settle it — gently, since it isn’t your dominant dosha.
mealCheck.rebalanceWhyGeneric: Chosen to ease the extra {{dosha}} this meal added.
mealCheck.patternBalanced: Your recent meals sit fairly balanced.
